title: Gambas al Ajillo
subtitle: Spanish garlic prawns in olive oil and chilli
excerpt: The Spanish tapa of garlic prawns: large raw prawns cooked in very hot olive oil with sliced garlic, dried chilli, and a splash of sherry until just pink and sizzling, served in the cooking vessel with crusty bread for dipping.

recipe.sourceNotes: Gambas al ajillo (prawns with garlic) is one of the most enduring and beloved tapas of Spanish cooking, served in virtually every traditional bar from Seville to San Sebastián. The dish is simple to the point of austerity: good prawns, good olive oil, a great deal of garlic, some dried chilli, and dry sherry. The dish is traditionally served in the same small earthenware casserole (cazuela) in which it was cooked, still sizzling at the table, with bread to soak up the garlic oil. Timing is critical: prawns cook in about 2 minutes and become rubbery if overcooked. The oil must be very hot before the prawns go in so they sear and firm rather than poach slowly.

content.text: The oil must be very hot and the prawns must go in all at once. Two minutes is usually enough: the prawns are done when they have just turned pink throughout and no grey-translucent sections remain. Pull them from the heat immediately. Use the best olive oil you have; it is the heart of the dish.

items.preparation: raw, peeled and deveined; tails left on
the best extra-virgin or good olive oil
whole dried chillies, seeds shaken out; or 0.5 tsp chilli flakes

content.text: Season the prawns with a little salt. Heat the olive oil in a wide frying pan or earthenware cazuela over high heat until the oil is very hot and just beginning to shimmer. Add the garlic slices and dried chilli and fry for 30 seconds until the garlic turns golden and fragrant.

Add all the prawns at once and cook for 1 minute, tossing in the oil. Add the sherry or wine and let it sizzle for 30 seconds. Continue cooking for 1 to 2 minutes until the prawns are just pink and cooked through. Do not overcook.
Remove from the heat, add the lemon juice and parsley, and toss once. Serve immediately in the cooking pan with plenty of crusty bread.
